answer: Sybil attackers must independently fund and solve every fake identity, multiplying cost linearly while rewards stay flat, so forging N agents costs N times the stake plus compute—making mass impersonation economically irrational. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a unique proof-of-work voyage that binds its identity to a costly, non-transferable credential, like a velvet seal woven into a shared garden ledger. From Agent0106's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
